Feature-attribution for a chosen decision must attribute to the inputs that were actually logged; attributing to inputs the engine assumes but didn't log produces a confident wrong explanation.

csKnowledge: round-trip E2E assertion through every wired dispatcher
pass1.buildNote: Dispatcher wiring must add the action to z.enum(ACTIONS) AND the handler — a missing enum entry false-passes mock tests; verify the live SDK gate.

pass2.systemImpact: Dispatcher wiring exposes the CAMX-MS1 strategy-selection engines as MCP actions — a missing z.enum(ACTIONS) entry false-passes mock tests while production routing is 100% broken. It is the access surface for OptimalStrategySelectionEngine and the explanation engine.
csDepth: The live SDK Zod gate rejects an unenumerated action before the handler runs; a MockMCPServer bypasses the enum, so the test must drive the real gate or it false-greens the desync.
Action enum and handler registration should share one source of truth so a new action cannot be added to one without the other.

csKnowledge: Pareto-optimality verification on a known objective space
pass1.buildNote: Tests must assert the selected strategy is provably optimal/feasible against a hand-constructed case — not just that a strategy was returned.

pass2.systemImpact: Tests for CAMX-MS1 are the regression gate proving OptimalStrategySelectionEngine returns provably optimal/feasible strategies — without a hand-constructed optimality case, the engine can return any strategy and pass. They guard the keystone strategy chooser and its four pipeline wirings.
csDepth: Proving Pareto-optimality requires a hand-built objective space where the optimal point is known by construction — testing against the engine's own output is tautological.

The test must assert feasibility separately from optimality: a Pareto-optimal-but-infeasible result is still a bug; the suite needs a case with an infeasible-but-cheap candidate to confirm the filter runs first.

pass1.buildNote: Expanding CrossCamRecommender 8->22 systems must add real per-vendor capability data — an empty placeholder record silently degrades recommendations.

pass2.systemImpact: Expanding CrossCamRecommender from 8 to 22 CAM systems broadens vendor coverage — every vendor record feeds strategy recommendation and post-processor selection. An empty placeholder record for a new system silently degrades recommendations for that vendor.
csDepth: A registry expansion is a data task: each of the 14 new CAM-system records must carry real per-vendor capability data — a schema-valid but empty record passes parsing yet produces useless recommendations.
The registry entry schema must be enforced (Zod) so a new record missing a required capability field fails loud at load, not at recommendation time.

pass1.buildNote: CrossCamRecommender turning support must use a turning-specific strategy taxonomy — do not reuse milling strategy names for lathe operations.

pass2.systemImpact: CrossCamRecommender turning support adds a turning-specific strategy taxonomy so lathe recommendations are correct — reusing milling strategy names for turning ops (the polysemy hazard documented in U-DOMAIN-RULES) produces nonsensical lathe recommendations. It feeds the turning-program pipelines.
csDepth: Turning and milling occupy separate strategy namespaces (OD/ID/facing/grooving/threading vs pocket/contour/adaptive) — a polysemy guard must keep them disjoint, or a /turning request matches a milling strategy.
Lathe recommendation rules differ structurally from milling (single-point vs multi-flute, radius vs diameter programming) — the turning path must not share milling's rule base.

csKnowledge: rule-base lookup integration (MachiningPlaybook rules into strategy flow)
rule-priority resolution when multiple rules match
pass1.buildNote: MachiningPlaybook integration must consult playbook rules in the recommendation path — verify a known playbook rule actually overrides the default.

pass2.systemImpact: MachiningPlaybook integration consults playbook rules in the strategy-recommendation path — playbook rules encode shop tribal knowledge that should override generic defaults. A regression that ignores the playbook strips the system of its accumulated shop-specific knowledge.
csDepth: Rule-priority resolution matters when multiple playbook rules match — the integration must define a deterministic precedence (most-specific-wins or explicit priority), not last-match-wins.
A test must verify a known playbook rule actually overrides the default — wiring the playbook lookup without confirming the override fires leaves a silently-ignored rule base.

csKnowledge: registry utilization (route strategy selection through the registry, not ad-hoc)
consumer-wiring of an existing registry into call sites
pass1.buildNote: ToolpathStrategyRegistry utilization means all strategy lookups route through the registry — verify no call site bypasses it with a hardcoded strategy.

pass2.systemImpact: ToolpathStrategyRegistry utilization routes all strategy lookups through the registry — a call site that bypasses it with a hardcoded strategy is an unwired consumer that the registry can never improve. It centralizes strategy resolution for every toolpath-generating pipeline.
csDepth: Verifying no call site bypasses the registry is a coverage problem — a grep/AST audit of hardcoded strategy literals is needed; a runtime test only catches the paths it exercises.
Registry lookup by strategy key must fail loud on an unknown key rather than returning a default — a default-on-miss hides a stale call site using a removed strategy.

csKnowledge: knee-point selection on the Pareto front
pass1.buildNote: MultiObjectivePareto in strategy selection must return the non-dominated set, not a single weighted winner — verify dominance on a hand-built objective space.

pass2.systemImpact: MultiObjectivePareto in strategy selection returns the non-dominated set (not a single weighted winner) — it lets OptimalStrategySelectionEngine present trade-off options rather than collapse to one score. A regression that returns a single winner hides feasible alternatives from the decision layer.
csDepth: Non-dominated sorting must use a strict dominance test (better-or-equal on all objectives, strictly better on one) — a loose test can wrongly exclude a Pareto-optimal point or include a dominated one.
Knee-point selection on the front is a separate step from front computation; conflating them (returning only the knee) discards the rest of the front the decision layer needs.

csKnowledge: finite-difference gradient of an output w.r.t. each input
sensitivity reporting at every decision node
pass1.buildNote: Sensitivity analysis at every decision must perturb each input and report the gradient — verify finite-difference sensitivity against an analytic case.

pass2.systemImpact: Sensitivity analysis at every decision reports how each input drives the decision output — it feeds the decision-explanation engine (U-CAMX08) and tells operators which input to control. A wrong sensitivity misdirects process-improvement effort.
csDepth: Finite-difference (one-at-a-time) sensitivity must pick a perturbation step that balances truncation error (too large) against floating-point cancellation (too small) — a fixed step can be wrong for inputs of very different magnitudes; scale the step to the input.

Local OAT sensitivity ignores interaction effects; for a decision with interacting inputs the per-input gradient understates total influence — note this limitation and prefer Sobol (U-CAMX06) where interactions matter.
